text.p: The following are the leading stories in the local press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- More than 1,000 tenants under the Malawi Housing Corporation (MHC) in Blantyre vowed to fight against the 90 percent rent rise and resolved to contribute K100 each for hiring a lawyer to contest the matter in court.
- The opposition Alliance For Democracy's (AFORD) executive council is expected to meet in Lilongwe this weekend to endorse a merger with the main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP).

- High Court Judge Duncan Tambala has sued a secondary school teacher and his employer, the Ministry of Education and Culture, for beating up his daughter in Blantyre against the country's policy on corporal punishment.

- Police said on Tuesday they were investigating a case of K1.7 million ($113,000) which went missing from the Commercial Bank of Malawi (CBM) in a spate of bank raids by a syndicate of unscrupulous people fraudulently syphoning them of hard cash.

- The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) sharply criticised the Malawi Posts and Telecommunications Corporation (MPTC) for granting a licence to a private U.S. firm to operate a commercial internet system when it had offered to operate the same system cheaply.
